title: One More Setup
summary: Veyra admits that one of Samuel's planted identities is still waiting ahead at Bellweather: Elias Bell, the estranged son of a woman whose wake has already begun. Kael could avoid the place, but chooses to go because someone has already put his face inside a grieving family's business.

panelPlan.text: At a roadside camp, Veyra lays Samuel's old route notes on a blanket. One remaining name is circled: ELIAS BELL — BELLWEATHER.
Samuel explains that he spoke to one cousin before the relay confrontation. He has not been back and cannot pull the story out again.
Kael folds the note once and hands it back. Eva expects him to detour. Instead he asks how far Bellweather is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: There's one more place we can't get ahead of.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: You mean one more place you already got ahead of.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Bellweather. I told one cousin that Elias Bell might come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Who is Elias Bell?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: A son who left years ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: And you gave them Kael.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I gave them a description.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: How far?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: You want to go there?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: If they're waiting for me because of him, I would rather they hear the truth from me than spend another week waiting.

directionInline.text: The setup is already in motion; Veyra and Samuel are not continuing the experiment here. Kael goes because the manipulation created a human obligation, not because he suddenly wants to solve the mystery.

title: The Wake
summary: Bellweather is in the middle of Mara Bell's mother's three-day wake, when unresolved promises to the dead are spoken aloud. Mara and Owen see Kael and immediately pull him into the absent Elias's place in the family.

panelPlan.text: Bellweather is a clustered family settlement around a shaded courtyard. Food, chairs and sleeping children make the wake feel lived-in rather than ceremonial spectacle.
Mara Bell sees Kael at the gate and stops with a serving bowl in both hands. Owen rises more slowly, angry before he is convinced.
Kael removes his hat out of ordinary respect for the wake and tells them his name before either sibling can finish welcoming Elias home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mara Bell
dialogueInline.text: Elias?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: No, ma’am. My name is Kael Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Owen Bell
dialogueInline.text: He said you would deny it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Of course he did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Eva.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mara Bell
dialogueInline.text: You have his face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm sorry. I don't have the rest of him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Owen Bell
dialogueInline.text: Convenient.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Not especially.

directionInline.text: The wake must remain a family event first. Kael's politeness matters: he does not mock their grief or turn the mistake into a performance.

title: What the Dead Promised
summary: The Bell siblings' real conflict surfaces. Their mother promised a tenant family permanent use of two houses, but Owen claims only Elias heard the promise and therefore only Elias can settle it. Kael refuses to become the missing witness.

panelPlan.text: At the long wake table, Mara states the promise while Owen insists there is no written record. Other relatives listen because the decision will affect people they know.
Owen pushes a family token toward Kael and asks Elias to say what their mother told him. Kael does not touch it.
Eva watches how easily one sentence from Kael could end the argument; Jessa watches Kael instead of the table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Owen Bell
dialogueInline.text: You were there when she promised it. Say what she said.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mara Bell
dialogueInline.text: If you would just tell him—

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Ma’am, if I tell him what you want to hear, you will still have the same problem tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You could help them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I can help them. I can't be Elias for them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Owen Bell
dialogueInline.text: Then what good are you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: At the moment? Another person telling you your sister is standing right here.

directionInline.text: This is the first explicit temptation to use an assigned identity for a good outcome. Kael's refusal is ethical rather than stubborn: a useful lie would become part of the community after he leaves.

title: The Useful Lie
summary: Eva argues privately that Kael could pretend for five minutes and spare the family a fight. Jessa pushes back, and the disagreement becomes the first time the women clearly reveal different instincts through their theories about him.

panelPlan.text: Behind the Bell house, Eva catches Kael and Jessa near the water jars while the wake continues inside.
Eva makes the practical case for one harmless performance. Kael listens longer than she expects before answering.
Jessa points out that Eva is treating the end of the scene as the end of the consequence. Eva realizes Jessa is defending Kael's position, and teases her about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Five minutes. You say you heard the promise, they stop fighting, and we leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: And next year somebody asks what else Elias said.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Maybe nobody does.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. But if they do, we're gone and they're stuck with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You sound like him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Don't start.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I was about to say she sounded sensible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Of course you were.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Please stop helping me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: All right.

directionInline.text: Let Eva and Jessa genuinely disagree without making either foolish. Their debate about Kael is also a debate about consequence, responsibility and how far ahead each of them thinks.

title: The Detail Samuel Missed
summary: Mara mentions that the man who prepared them for Elias also knew a private Bell family phrase Samuel insists he never heard or repeated. Veyra arrives expecting to audit her own setup and instead finds evidence that the story had acquired information outside her control.

panelPlan.text: Veyra and Samuel reach Bellweather late in the wake. Mara is furious when she recognizes Samuel's coat.
She repeats the phrase Samuel used: 'the blue room stays open.' Samuel goes still because the phrase was not in his notes and Mara says she had not told him what it meant.
Veyra checks Samuel's old page anyway. Kael does not crowd the discovery; he is helping carry chairs back under the awning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mara Bell
dialogueInline.text: You told me Elias would remember the blue room stays open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: No. I told you Elias might come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mara Bell
dialogueInline.text: You said those words.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Did she tell you what they meant?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I never heard them before tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So either one of you is lying—

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Or somebody else was already in the story.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Could you have this argument after we put the tables away?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: How are you not more bothered by this?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I'm bothered. The tables are still in the rain.

directionInline.text: The extra detail is evidence, not proof of magic. Keep multiple human possibilities open: memory, another visitor, deliberate deception, or a source Veyra and Samuel do not know.

title: After the Wake
summary: The Bell family resolves the housing promise through living witnesses and their own willingness to honor it, not through Kael impersonating Elias. Kael explains to Eva why the lie would have been worse precisely because it might have worked.

panelPlan.text: An elderly aunt confirms enough of the dead woman's promise that Mara and Owen can decide what they are willing to honor. The tenant family is present but not reduced to props.
Outside after the wake, Eva sits on the rig step while Kael washes a borrowed plate. Jessa listens without pretending not to.
Veyra and Samuel remain behind speaking with Mara about the unexplained phrase. The trio leaves before their investigation turns the wake back into a test.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It would have been easier if you had lied.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: For us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: For them too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Tonight, maybe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And tomorrow?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow they'd remember Elias came home and said it. I'd be gone, but that wouldn't be.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: That's what I meant.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You said something about legs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I was trying not to make a speech.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I appreciated the effort.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Drive.

directionInline.text: End on character rather than clue. The mystery advances, but Kael's ethics and the Eva/Jessa relationship are the durable change.
